project_announced_description: This USDA Rural Development investment will be used by the city of Prairie Du Chien for the construction of a new joint facility for the police and fire departments. The current two existing stations are no longer suitably meeting the current needs in size, construction, or design to continue to provide invaluable services for the community. This new facility will include a large training and fitness room that will be shared by both departments. The police department portion will include vehicle storage and office space, while the fire department will include apparatus bays, decontamination space, living quarters and office spaces. The replacement facility will house both departments in one location to allow better cooperation and decrease infrastructure costs.

project_announced_description: This USDA Rural Development investment will be used by the city of Viroqua to install an active gas system to mitigate their closed landfill that has gas migrating offsite and exceeding allowable limits established by the Wisconsin Department of Natural Resources (WDNR). Viroqua currently owns the town dump that started in the mid-1960s. This waste dump stopped accepting waste in 1992 and was closed by installing a clay cap, surface water controls and a passive gas system. In 2025, gas was discovered migrating offsite to the entire surrounding area including methane gas, and the city of Viroqua was issued a Notice of Noncompliance by WDNR. To address this problem, the city will install an active gas system that will include installing up to 60 gas wells that are drilled and connected to a gas blower that will draw gas out of the wells and feed it to a flare. This gas system will help the city alleviate the notice issued by WDNR and address health and safety concerns of gas moving and accumulating in nearby homes and businesses where it could concentrate and become explosive.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to renovate the city of Lancaster's existing fire and rescue station. The 28 years old existing station serves as headquarters for the Lancaster Fire Department and Lancaster Emergency Medical System (EMS). Interior renovations will include heating and cooling, plumbing, power distribution and back-up power supply. Interior/emergency lighting, Wi-Fi, security equipment, sleeping areas, gear storage, decontamination laundry, showers, an office area, commercial kitchen equipment, and workout area are also being added inside the facility. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to allow Dramm Corporation to increase the production of nitrogen-based fertilizer and expand its customer/farmer network in the United States. The funds will be used to modernize equipment used in production, purchase climate-smart equipment to reduce greenhouse gases and construct an additional building allowing Dramm to increase production capacity utilizing the existing site adjacent to current production facility. Using fish offal (heads, bones, racks, and viscera) collected from commercial and sport fishermen of the Great Lakes, Dramm produces a liquid fish fertilizer suitable for organic and traditional farming alike while keeping millions of pounds of waste out of landfills and fresh waterways. Dramm is heavily focused on sustainability, preservation, and employee safety. A solar array will be added to the fertilizer location which will power approximately 55% of the production machinery. Replacing the outdated forklifts with LP forklifts with tote grabbers will increase employee safety. The purchase of a new box truck with lift gate will ensure reliable and increased collection of offal supply for production. All of Dramm s expansion plans are focused on increasing production to increase distribution to farmers, employee safety and reducing our carbon footprint.

naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to provide additional financing for the upgrades to the village of Sharon wastewater treatment facility (WWTF). The village plans to replace mechanical and electrical instrumentation, aeration blowers, pumps, clarifier equipment, fiberglass dome structure and add additional sludge storage. Upgrades will also include new phosphorus treatment equipment that will be needed to meet new water quality related phosphorus treatment requirements. The current WWTF has no treatment for the incoming phosphorus. The collection system dates to the 1920's and consists of several sewer mains, manholes and service laterals that need replacement and upgrades. These improvements are needed more than ever due to high intensity rain events that caused major flooding and resulted in sanitary sewer backups.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to construct a fire station. The fire department provides service not only to the city of Platteville, but also to all or portions of the townships of Platteville, Smelser, Lima, Harrison and Ellenboro in Grant County, and townships of Elk Grove and Belmont in Lafayette County. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to upgrade the water system and wells. Well #1 (constructed in 1933 and reconstructed in 1984) and Well #3 (constructed in 1982) are both subject to a growth of natural biofilm with acid producing bacteria. This change in the water chemistry increases the solubility of manganese and thus the manganese levels of the well water poses a very dangerous risk to the village residents and leaves the water undrinkable. The upgrade and rehabilitation will help reduce corrosion of the pump and well casing in each well and corrosion of lead pipe and copper plumbing in the water distribution system, thus being able to control acceptable manganese levels in drinking water to the residents. The Village will also be receiving funding from the WI Department of Natural Resources for additional sewer and water improvements.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to construct a community anaerobic digester in Brown County, Wisconsin. Feedstock will be pumped to the facility via pipeline from two farms and trucked to the facility from the remaining ten.Two biproducts of this process will be potable water and fiber that will be returned to the farms that provide the feedstock for use as animal bedding. BC Organics process consists of three key technologies: anaerobic digestion, biogas upgrading and cleanup, and nutrient recovery and water reclamation.

naics_industry_sector: Construction
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will beused to construct a new street to serve a new development area located in the village of Ontario. The village has experienced reoccurring flooding which has caused significant damage to the infrastructure and business community and creates a serious health & safety hazard. The village plans to implement a flood relocation project to avoid the negative impact caused by future floods.The proposed project consists of creating new building sites on high ground that will be resilient to natural disasters and provide necessary infrastructure to support a sustainable community. The new development areas will provide sites for businesses, multi- family residential and single-family residential development.

funding_code: CF 2019 DISASTER GRANT - TORNADOES FLOODS OTHER
naics_industry_sector: Construction
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used to purchase a new tractor loader with accessories.The villages 2003 backhoe has limited capabilities due to its size and has become a high maintenance vehicle due to extensive use. This project includes the purchase of a new compact truck loader with snow blower and brush cat attachments. This piece of equipment will be used to remove sand/silt and debris after flood events and storms. The brush hog will aid in controlling brush growth along the Kickapoo River and the snow blower attachment will be used to blow snow directly from the street on to trucks. This new equipment will increase efficiency and reduce costs for the Village while providing needed services for the residents.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will provide additional financing for the Wastewater Treatment Facility (WWTF) project funded in Fiscal Year 2019. project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment provides additional funding for the initial lagoon improvement project funded in 2018. The existing lagoon wastewater treatment facility, used to treat and dispose of wastewater generated throughout the reservation, has been identified by Indian Health Services (IHS) as having several deficiencies including negative impacts to local groundwater quality and does not have sufficient capacity to support future development plans. funding_code: (GRANT ONLY) 306C-NATIVE AMERICAN-WATER ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used by the Bad River Tribe to assist in the improvement of the community water systems for the Franks Field (FF) and Birch Hill (BH) areas of the reservation, which were installed in phases since 1960 and have many components that do not meet current design standards. Both areas have insufficient well storage capacities that affect their ability to meet full fire flow and the pump house is outdated and lacks a backup source of power. This project will include improvements to the wells at FF including a new pump house and water tower, an interconnecting water main to connect BH to FF, as once improvements are made at FF they will adequately be able to supply both communities. Also included will be the demolition of the existing FF water tower, BH pump house and abandonment of the existing BH wells.

funding_code: (COMB LOAN & GRANT) WASTE DISPOSAL ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development will be used by the Town of Sullivan S.D. #1 to upgrade the existing Wastewater Treatment Facility (WWTF) to provide treatment for both the District and the nearby Village of Sullivan. The existing WWTF, built in 1978-1979, is reaching the end of its useful life and is in need of replacement or upgrades to ensure a reliable system, as well as to provide a safe working environment. The existing District WWTF does not have phosphorus treatment capabilities and will need to be upgraded to meet new effluent phosphorus limits. This project will be constructed at the existing WWTF site as it has adequate space to construct a regional facility. The Village of Sullivan will construct a new lift station and force main to convey wastewater from the Village to the regional WWTF. Upgrades include: renovation of Administration/Lab building, main lift station renovation, new headworks building, new activated sludge package plant and new clarifiers to provide secondary treatment and biological phosphorus removal. This project is being done in conjunction with the Village of Sullivan WWTF upgrade also funded thru RD in FY19.

funding_code: (COMB LOAN & GRANT) WASTE DISPOSAL ONLY
naics_industry_sector: Utilities
project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used by the Village of Maine to upgrade the Villages wastewater collection system. The older/east side of the collection system is composed of 8" clay piping and brick/block manholes. Inspections of this area revealed that the sewers have leaking joints, invasive roots and cracks in the piping. The manholes need repair or replacement due to deteriorating conditions. In addition, a 50-year-old pumping station on Everest Avenue is located in the right-of-way making safe access difficult and is need of replacement due to deteriorated piping, valves and structure. This project would include replacement of the existing sewers on the east side of the Village with new PVC piping and the existing manholes with new precast concrete manholes. Replacement of the sewer and manholes will significantly decrease infiltration and inflow into the collection system. The Everest Avenue lift station will be relocated to allow for safe access and will include above ground controls in a weather-proof enclosure providing access to the controls without confined space entry.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used by Shawano Area Matthew 25, Inc. (SAM25) to purchase equipment for a seasonal emergency homeless shelter. SAM25s mission is to help those affected by poverty improve their circumstances and become self-sufficient. Due to the increased use and number of those in need in the Shawano area, SAM25 recently purchased a new, enlarged facility that will be able to accommodate and help more individuals and families. Funds for this project would be used to purchase furniture for the new facility including: metal frame beds and bed bug resistant mattresses; couches and chairs for the communal areas; dining room tables and chairs; resource room furnishings including training tables and chairs to provide quests with education and support; and technology for safety and support including security cameras, desk monitors, and computers for intake process. Also needed are office furnishings, kitchen and laundry appliances, entry intercom and doorbell system, and furniture for the childrens play area. This project would serve Shawano as well as the surrounding area.

project_announced_description: This Rural Development investment will be used by the Village of Ontario to research the implementation of a flood mitigation project to avoid the negative impact caused by future floods. The Kickapoo River has flooded the Village in 2007, 2008, 2010 and 2018 with the 2018 flood reaching an elevation of four feet above the 100-year flood level. Damage affected the fire station, community center, Village infrastructure, 19 of 25 businesses and 11 houses. The funds will support investigations necessary to determine what work is required to improve the waste water collection and treatment system and possible relocation into Ontario. The proposed relocation project consists of creating new building sites on high ground that will be resilient to natural disasters and provide necessary infrastructure to support a sustainable community, including land acquisition, site grading and extension of the Village streets, sanitary sewer, water main and storm sewer. Upon completion of the project, the Village will have available sites for existing businesses and residents to move to, plus accommodate new businesses and residential development in the future.
